on 23 March, 2023
 The Hon'Ble Sri Justice V.Gopala Krishna Rao
 M.A.C.M.A. No.2995 of 2012
Judgement:
The appellant is the third respondent in M.V.O.P.No.413 of 2004 on the file of the Iv Additional
Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (Fast Track Court), Nellore and
the respondents are the petitioner and respondents 1 and 2 in the said case.
2. Both the parties in the appeal will be referred to as they are arrayed in claim application.

3. The claimant filed a Claim Petition under sections 166 and 140 of Motor Vehicles Act against the respondents by praying the Tribunal to award an amount of Rs.1,25,000/- towards compensation for the injuries sustained by the petitioner in a Motor Vehicle Accident occurred on 01.08.2003.

4. The case of the claimant is that the petitioner is a cleaner of the lorry bearing No.AP 31T 1961 and on 01.08.2003 at about 11.00 p.m., while the petitioner was on the duty, the petitioner and driver and co-driver returning from Cuddapah to Guntur with empty pepsi VGKRJ MACMA 2995 of 2012 bottles load, the driver of lorry lost control over the vehicle and the vehicle was skidded, resulting which the petitioner sustained grievous injuries and the petitioner claimed an amount of Rs.1,25,000/- towards compensation for the injuries sustained by him.

5. The third respondent filed counter by denying the claim application and contended that the claimant is not entitled any compensation and the third respondent is not liable to pay any compensation to the petitioner.

6. Based on the above pleadings, the Tribunal framed the following issues:
i. Whether the pleaded accident was occurred due to the fault of the driver of the lorry bearing No.AP 31T 1961 and that the driver of the said lorry was having valid driving licence as on the material date of accident?
ii. Whether there was valid insurance policy obtained for the accident lorry No.AP 31T 1961 as on the material date of accident?

iii. Whether the vehicle, the lorry bearing No.AP 31 T1961 is the vehicle involved in the pleaded VGKRJ MACMA 2995 of 2012 accident and not the lorry bearing No.AP 31T 1961 as pleaded by the 3rd respondent?

iv. Whether the petitioner is received any injuries in the pleaded accident and whether he is entitled to any compensation, if so, at what rate and against which of the respondents?
v.
To what relief?
7. On behalf of the petitioner, PW1 and PW2 were examined and Ex.A1 to Ex.A3 and Ex.X1 and Ex.X2 were marked.
On behalf of third respondent RW1 was examined and Ex.B1 was marked.

8. After considering the evidence on record, the Tribunal has given a finding that the accident was occurred due to rash and negligent driving of driver of offending vehicle and the Tribunal granted an amount of Rs.75,000/- to the claimant towards compensation.
9. Aggrieved by the same, the third respondent/ Insurance company filed the present appeal.

10. Now, the point for consideration is:
 Whether the Order of Tribunal needs any  interference?
VGKRJ MACMA 2995 of 2012 11. POINT:-

The case of the petitioner is that he is a cleaner of the lorry bearing No.AP 31T 1961 working under the first respondent and on 01.08.2003 at about 23.00 hours, while the petitioner was on the duty, the petitioner, driver and co-driver returning from Cuddapah to Guntur with empty pepsi bottles load, the driver of lorry lost control over the vehicle and the vehicle was skidded, resulting which the petitioner sustained grievous and fracture injuries and he admitted in the hospital.
12. In order to prove the case of the petitioner, the petitioner himself was examined as PW1.

As per his evidence, he was a cleaner of lorry bearing No.AP 31T 1961 and on 01.08.2003 at 11.00 p.m. while they were in return trip from Cuddapah to Guntur with empty pepsi bottles load, the driver of the lorry lost control over the vehicle and the vehicle was skidded, due to the accident, he received injuries and he sustained fracture injury and he was admitted in Government Hospital, Cuddapah, later he was shifted to Government Hospital, Nellore for better treatment.
PW1 is the injured person, who received injuries in the accident and he is the best person to speak about National Insurance Company Limited vs Manukonda Samba Siva Rao Samba Sivaiah 2 ...

the rash and negligent driving of the VGKRJ MACMA 2995 of 2012 driver of the crime vehicle/ lorry bearing No.AP 31 T 1961.

Ex.A1 certified copy of First Information Report shows that the driver of crime vehicle drove the same in a rash and negligent manner and after completion of investigation, the police also filed charge sheet under Ex.A3 against the driver of the crime vehicle and the first respondent is the owner of the said crime vehicle/ lorry, second respondent is the insured and the third respondent is the insurer of the lorry/ crime vehicle.
13.
The petitioner also examined one S.Venkateswara Raju, who is the then Head Constable of Kavali Rural police station as PW2.

As per his evidence, at present he is working as Assistant Sub Inspector of Police, Jaladanki,
previously, he worked as Head Constable at Kavali rural police station.
As per his evidence, on the date of accident, the petitioner was cleaner of offending vehicle and charge sheet was filed against the driver of the lorry.
Therefore, the evidence on record proves that the accident was occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the lorry bearing No.AP 31 T 1961.
In order to prove the claim of the petitioner, the petitioner also relied on Ex.A2 certified copy of wound certificate.
VGKRJ MACMA 2995 of 2012 14.

The contention of the Insurance Company is that Ex.B1 policy was insured by second respondent and at the request of insured, the crime vehicle lorry was transferred to Sri P.Masthan Vali/ 1 st respondent.

Therefore, as per the evidence on record, the first respondent is the owner of the said lorry and Ex.B1 insurance policy also discloses that the insured name is P.Masthan Vali/ 1 st respondent and the offending vehicle number also noted in Ex.B1.
As per Ex.B1, the first respondent was the owner of the lorry and the policy was also on force by the date of accident.
RW1 admitted in cross examination that the vehicle was validly insured under Ex.B1 policy and he also admits as per Ex.X2, the claimant is shown as cleaner.
15. Ex.A2 attested xerox copy of wound certificate clearly goes to show that the petitioner sustained one grievous injury and one simple injury.
The learned Tribunal without giving any cogent reasons simply granted an amount of Rs.75,000/- towards compensation from first and third respondents herein.
As per the evidence on record, the claimant sustained one grievous injury and one simple injury.

Therefore, an amount of Rs.20,000/- is awarded to the claimant for one grievous injury and an amount of Rs.5,000/-
VGKRJ MACMA 2995 of 2012 is awarded for one simple injury.
The claim petitioner sustained one grievous injury and one simple injury, therefore an amount of Rs.30,000/- is awarded towards pain and suffering.
Since the petitioner sustained one grievous injury and one simple injury and he was hospitalized for a long time, therefore an amount of Rs.10,000/- is granted towards loss of income.
In view of the injury sustained by the petitioner an amount of Rs.10,000/- is awarded towards transportation charges and nutrition of food.
In total, the claimant is entitled an amount of Rs.75,000/- from the first respondent, who is the owner of the vehicle.

PW2/ Investigating Officer admitted in his cross examination that as per the charge sheet, the claim petitioner is the passenger of the offending vehicle.

The contention of the Insurance Company is that the claimant is travelling in the offending vehicle as an unauthorized passenger and therefore there is a violation of policy and that Insurance Company is not liable to pay any compensation.

17. Here the claim petitioner, who is the cleaner of offending vehicle, is travelling in the lorry at the time of accident and in view of VGKRJ MACMA 2995 of 2012 the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the lorry, he sustained injuries in a road accident and the first respondent is the owner of the lorry and the crime vehicle lorry is insured with the third respondent by the first respondent and the policy is also in force and in view of the decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court of India (three Judge Bench) of Singh ram Vs., Nirmala and others 1 , the Insurance Company shall pay the claim at first instance and later recover the same from the owner of the crime vehicle.

sentences.text: In the judgment of Manuara Khatun and others Vs. Rajesh Kumar Singh and others2 it was held that the direction to United India Insurance Company Limited being the insurer of the offending vehicle which was found involved in causing accident due to negligence of its driver needs to be issued directing them (United India Insurance Company Limited/ respondent No.3) to first pay the awarded sum to the appellants (claimants) and then to recover the paid awarded sum from the owner of the offending vehicle without filing any independent suit by filing an Execution Petition against the 2018 Law Suit (SC) 191, (2017) 4 Supreme Court Cases 796 VGKRJ MACMA 2995 of 2012 owner of the crime vehicle.

sentences.text: Therefore, third respondent is directed to pay the entire compensation of Rs.75,000/- to the claimant at first instance, later recover the same from the first respondent, who is the owner of the crime vehicle.

18. Accordingly, the 3rd respondent/ Insurance company is directed to pay the total claim of Rs.75,000/- to the claimant at first instance, later recover the same from respondent No.1 by filing Execution Petition without filing independent suit, since the first respondent is the owner of the offending vehicle at the time of accident.

19. In the result, this appeal is disposed of, by modifying the order dated 17.08.2011 passed in M.V.O.P.No.413 of 2004 on the file of the IV Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (Fast Track Court), Nellore.

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: It is held that the claimant is entitled to a total compensation of Rs.75,000/- with interest @7.5% p.a., from the date of petition, till the date of payment.

The 3rd respondent/
Insurance Company is directed to pay the claim amount, within one month from the date of this judgment, to the claimant at first VGKRJ MACMA 2995 of 2012 instance and later recover the same from respondent No.1 by filing an Execution Petition and without filing any independent suit.
On such deposit, the claimant is entitled to withdraw the same along with costs and accrued interest thereon.
There shall be no order as to costs.
Miscellaneous petitions, if any, pending in this appeal shall stand closed.
V.GOPALA KRISHNA RAO,J Dated: 23.03.2023.

The learned Tribunal without giving any cogent reasons simply granted an amount of Rs.75,000/- towards compensation from first and third respondents herein.
As per the evidence on record, the claimant sustained one grievous injury and one simple injury.
